title: Sikh Empire (1799-1849)
key_facts: Religious empire founded by Guru Nanak in 15th century
Peak under Maharaja Ranjit Singh controlling Punjab region
Military power challenged both Mughals and Afghans
Known for military organization and religious tolerance policies
causes: Religious reform movement challenging Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy
Mughal Empire's weakness after Maratha expansion
Military organization of Khalsa army by Guru Gobind Singh
Punjab's strategic location between Persian and Indian subcontinent
outcome: Empire fragmented after Ranjit Singh's death
Established Punjab as center of Sikh identity and culture
Legacy of religious syncretism and martial traditions
impacts: Established Sikhism as major world religion
Created Punjabi cultural and linguistic identity
Influenced Indian military traditions and organization
Left legacy of religious tolerance and martial arts
